historical_names.date_source_note: Official founding and public presentation of the coastal resort city of Pinamar by architect Jorge Bunge on 14 February 1943 on stabilised coastal dunes (Plan Director approved 1944; autonomous Partido de Pinamar created 1 July 1978).
historical_names.name: Pinamar

historical_names.date_source_note: Traditional colonial founding date (3 January 1647) of the hamlet of Santero near Cispatá Bay on ancestral Zenú territory by Diego de Corbella.
historical_names.name: Santero

historical_names.date_source_note: Official colonial refounding and urban layout as San Antero on 3 January 1777 by Captain Antonio de la Torre y Miranda.
historical_names.name: San Antero

historical_names.date_source_note: Establishment of Guardia del Salto (also Fuerte de San Antonio del Salto de los Arrecifes) on 21 June 1752 by the Blandengues company La Invencible on the Pampean frontier.
historical_names.name: Guardia del Salto

historical_names.date_source_note: Creation of the modern Partido de Salto on 25 October 1854, consolidating the civil town under the name Salto.
historical_names.name: Salto

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial highland settlement and Inca tambo/fortress incorporated into Tawantinsuyu in the late 15th century on Caxas/Guayacundo territory, documented during the 1532 Spanish advance toward Cajamarca (approximate pre-contact date); colonial parish of Santa Ana de Huarmaca and republican district created on 8 October 1840.
historical_names.name: Huarmaca

historical_names.date_source_note: Attested in the Fifth Uruguayan Population Census of 21 May 1975 as Rincón de la Bolsa, encompassing mid-20th-century coastal subdivisions in southern San José Department.
historical_names.name: Rincón de la Bolsa

historical_names.date_source_note: Officially designated and renamed Ciudad del Plata by Law No. 18.052 on 25 October 2006.
historical_names.name: Ciudad del Plata

historical_names.date_source_note: Colonial foundation as San Miguel de Villeta by Alonso de Olalla and Hernando de Alcocer
historical_names.name: San Miguel de Villeta

historical_names.date_source_note: Republican-era official municipal name Villeta
historical_names.name: Villeta

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded and erected as a municipality under the name Aguazul by Boyacá Departmental Decree No. 295 on 5 April 1954 (ratified April 1956), succeeding the ruined town of Sevilla on the Únete River.
historical_names.name: Aguazul

historical_names.date_source_note: Coastal settlement established by Colonche migrants; parish 1861
historical_names.name: Manglaralto

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial indigenous Patías territory and valley settlement prior to Spanish conquest (approximate pre-contact date; colonial San Miguel de Patía attempted in 1749).
historical_names.name: Patía

historical_names.date_source_note: Municipal seat of El Bordo founded on 22 October 1824 by Friar José María Chacón y Sánchez.
historical_names.name: El Bordo

historical_names.date_source_note: Municipality of Patía formally erected by Departmental Ordinance No. 19 on 26 October 1907, with El Bordo as municipal seat.
historical_names.name: Patía

historical_names.date_source_note: Colonial founding of Concepción in Zulia (western shore of Lake Maracaibo) on 8 December 1752 under the ecclesiastical title Nuestra Señora Inmaculada de la Concepción de La Cañada.
historical_names.name: Nuestra Señora Inmaculada de la Concepción de La Cañada

historical_names.date_source_note: Recorded as the civil town and parish of Concepción in the First National Census of Venezuela (November 1873), later designated capital of Municipio La Cañada de Urdaneta (21 July 1989); input Yaracuy coordinates reflect upstream dataset conflation with the colonial curato of Taría.
historical_names.name: Concepción

historical_names.date_source_note: Modern settlement founded in 1963 around a Texas Petroleum Company oil camp on ancestral A'i Cofán and Siona territory (exact day/month unrecorded); erected as municipality by Decree 2891 of 28 December 1978.
historical_names.name: Orito

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial Pubenense indigenous predecessor settlement of Timbío prior to Spanish arrival (approximate pre-contact date).
historical_names.name: Timbío

historical_names.date_source_note: Spanish colonial founding on 1 November 1535 (All Saints' Day) by captains Juan de Ampudia and Pedro de Añasco under orders of Sebastián de Belalcázar, following the Battle of Mastales.
historical_names.name: Timbío

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial valley toponym at earliest dataset horizon
historical_names.name: Wilcapampa Yunca

historical_names.date_source_note: Colonial estate and parish; district created 1825
historical_names.name: Santa Ana

historical_names.date_source_note: Elevated to villa and provincial capital by Law 2890
historical_names.name: Quillabamba

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial indigenous coastal settlement of the Atacames/Mache culture on the Esmeraldas littoral prior to Spanish contact in 1526 (approximate pre-contact date); officially constituted as cantonal seat on 3 October 1956.
historical_names.name: Muisne

historical_names.date_source_note: Táchira piedmont settlement at earliest dataset horizon
historical_names.name: Boconó

historical_names.date_source_note: Agricultural colony founded in 1870 by Carlos Casado del Alisal as Colonia Candelaria on lands of Estancia Los Desmochados (exact day/month unrecorded).
historical_names.name: Colonia Candelaria

historical_names.date_source_note: Urban town centre laid out in 1873 as Villa Casilda within Colonia Candelaria (exact day/month unrecorded).
historical_names.name: Villa Casilda

historical_names.date_source_note: Elevated to city status under the name Casilda on 29 September 1907.
historical_names.name: Casilda

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial Tonocoté and Quechua-named thermal-springs site known as Inti Yacu ('Waters of the Sun') and Yacu Rúpaj prior to Spanish arrival (approximate pre-contact date).
historical_names.name: Inti Yacu

historical_names.date_source_note: First urban land surveys and early spa settlement at the paraje of Río Hondo in 1888 (exact day/month unrecorded).
historical_names.name: Río Hondo

historical_names.date_source_note: Official founding of the town of Termas de Río Hondo on 6 September 1954 (autonomous municipality created in 1958; town centre relocated following construction of the Dique Frontal in 1967).
historical_names.name: Termas de Río Hondo

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial Mapudungun toponym at earliest dataset horizon
historical_names.name: Curacaví

historical_names.date_source_note: Colonial waystation under encomienda of Juan Bautista Pastene
historical_names.name: Tambo Viejo de Puangue

historical_names.date_source_note: Documented as Curacaví under Melipilla from 1742; Curato 1767
historical_names.name: Curacaví

historical_names.date_source_note: District of Chancay (San Marcos Province, Cajamarca) created by Decree-Law No. 25853 on 16 November 1992 from former territory of Ichocán district.
historical_names.name: Chancay

historical_names.date_source_note: Afro-Venezuelan Yaracuy valley hamlet at dataset horizon
historical_names.name: Aldea Casimiro Vásquez

historical_names.date_source_note: Civil parish created in Veroes by Yaracuy gazette
historical_names.name: El Guayabo

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial Guayacundo/Ayahuaca chiefdom settlement incorporated into Tawantinsuyu prior to Spanish conquest (approximate pre-contact date).
historical_names.name: Ayahuaca

historical_names.date_source_note: Spanish colonial reducción founded in 1571 under the ecclesiastical title Nuestra Señora del Pilar de Ayavaca (exact day/month unrecorded; modern orthography Ayabaca).
historical_names.name: Ayabaca

historical_names.date_source_note: Modern settlement founded around 1878 (exact day/month unrecorded) on Carib/Chaima territory near the former 18th-century mission site of Nueva Palencia; became capital of Distrito (now Municipio) Bolívar on 30 January 1940.
historical_names.name: Caripito

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial Aymara altiplano settlement known as Llaxaa / Laxa prior to Inca and Spanish arrival (approximate pre-contact date).
historical_names.name: Llaxaa

historical_names.date_source_note: Site where Captain Alonso de Mendoza signed the founding act of Nuestra Señora de La Paz on 20 October 1548 before relocating the city to Chuquiago Marka days later; the altiplano town persisted under the Hispanicised name Laja.
historical_names.name: Laja

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial Muchik (Mochica/Chimú-era) settlement at Chuspo/Alicán within the Cinto chiefdom prior to Spanish colonial reduction (approximate pre-contact date; Muchik endonym later recorded as Omænssæfæc).
historical_names.name: Chuspo

historical_names.date_source_note: Colonial reducción de indios at Callanca (Cinto chiefdom), severely damaged by the 1578 El Niño floods and abandoned after the 1612 epidemic.
historical_names.name: Callanca

historical_names.date_source_note: Relocation and establishment of Monsefú (Hispanicised from Muchik Omænssæfæc) by survivors of the 1612 Callanca epidemic (exact day/month unrecorded); elevated to city on 26 October 1888.
historical_names.name: Monsefú

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 12 October 1953 by Lieutenant Jaime Fernández Salazar and displaced settlers from the ruined town of Moreno (earlier La Fragua), named for the 1953 Llanos peace accords; erected as a municipality on 12 October 1974.
historical_names.name: Paz de Ariporo

historical_names.date_source_note: Modern oil-camp settlement formally established in 1938 by Royal Dutch Shell / Venezuelan Oil Concessions on the eastern shore of Lake Maracaibo adjacent to ancestral indigenous palafito waters (exact day/month unrecorded); constituted as capital of the autonomous Municipality of Valmore Rodríguez in 1989 (law of 21 July 1989, implemented 11 December 1989 / 1989.12.11).
historical_names.name: Bachaquero

historical_names.date_source_note: Municipal seat Clarines founded on 1594-04-07 by Francisco de Vides (also associated with the Franciscan mission San Antonio de Clarines)
historical_names.name: San Antonio de Clarines

historical_names.date_source_note: Late 19th-century district created in honour of General Manuel Ezequiel Bruzual with seat at Clarines; exact creation day unverified
historical_names.name: Distrito Bruzual

historical_names.date_source_note: Constituted as autonomous Municipio Manuel Ezequiel Bruzual in Anzoátegui State in the early 1990s under Venezuela's municipal reform; exact decree day estimated
historical_names.name: Manuel Ezequiel Bruzual

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 20 January 1576 by Captain Francisco Redondo Ponce de León on Gorrones indigenous territory as Villa de Cáceres.
historical_names.name: Villa de Cáceres

historical_names.date_source_note: Relocated in 1602 (exact day/month unrecorded) to the Estancia de Roldanillo due to indigenous resistance, becoming San Sebastián de Roldanillo and subsequently Roldanillo.
historical_names.name: Roldanillo

historical_names.date_source_note: Erected as Municipio Castro on 29 July 1904 under President Cipriano Castro, with Las Tejerías as its seat.
historical_names.name: Castro

historical_names.date_source_note: Officially renamed Municipio Tejerías (later Municipio Foráneo Las Tejerías) in November 1909 following the fall of Cipriano Castro (exact day unrecorded).
historical_names.name: Tejerías

historical_names.date_source_note: Elevated to autonomous Municipio Autónomo Santos Michelena by the Legislative Assembly of Aragua State on 23 October 1986, retaining Las Tejerías as its capital.
historical_names.name: Santos Michelena

historical_names.date_source_note: Franciscan river mission and settlement of Puerto Ocopa consolidated in 1919 on ancestral Asháninka territory (exact day/month unrecorded), serving as initial administrative seat when Río Tambo District was created.
historical_names.name: Puerto Ocopa

historical_names.date_source_note: District of Río Tambo formally created by Law No. 9801 on 29 January 1943 (initially in Jauja Province, later Satipo Province), with Puerto Ocopa as provisional seat and subsequently Puerto Prado.
historical_names.name: Río Tambo
